title: Indian-Origin Muslim Man Stabbed 15 Times in Utah Mall in Hate Crime, Suspect Charged With Attempted Murder
excerpt: Prosecutors file two counts of attempted aggravated murder against a man who told police he 'intends to kill Muslims' after attacking an Indian kiosk worker at Valley Fair Mall.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Syed Sohail Uddin was stabbed 15 times in a Utah mall on July 13.
  • Suspect Peter Michael Larsen targeted Uddin due to his Islamic faith.
  • Larsen faces two counts of attempted aggravated murder with hate crime enhancements.
  • The Indian Consulate is providing assistance to Uddin's family.
  • The attack highlights rising anti-Muslim violence in the U.S.

Salt Lake County District Attorney
  • Syed Sohail Uddin, an Indian-origin Muslim man, was stabbed 15 times while working at a kiosk inside Valley Fair Mall in West Valley City, Utah on July 13
  • Suspect Peter Michael Larsen, 48, told police he targeted the victim because of his Islamic faith and said he "intends to kill Muslims"
  • Salt Lake County prosecutors have filed two counts of first-degree felony attempted aggravated murder with hate crime enhancements
  • The Consulate General of India in San Francisco confirmed it is providing consular assistance to the victim's family

An Indian-origin Muslim man was stabbed 15 times inside a Utah shopping mall on July 13 in what prosecutors are calling a premeditated hate crime. Syed Sohail Uddin, a kiosk worker at Valley Fair Mall in West Valley City, remains in critical condition and has undergone multiple surgeries for wounds to his hands, heart, and lungs.

Salt Lake County District Attorney Sim Gill announced on July 18 that Peter Michael Larsen, 48, has been charged with two counts of first-degree felony attempted aggravated murder. The charges include notices for a potential hate crime designation, habitual violent offender status, and use of a dangerous weapon by a restricted person.

The Attack

"Photo: Wikimedia Commons" style="max-width:100%;border-radius:8px" loading="lazy"><figcaption style="font-size:0.85rem;color:#666;margin-top:8px">San Francisco."

According to court documents and eyewitness accounts, Larsen approached the kiosk and asked the victim his name, where he was from, and whether he was Muslim. When Uddin confirmed his faith, Larsen asked for a bottle of water. As Uddin turned to retrieve it, the suspect pulled a knife and began stabbing him repeatedly.

Bystanders inside the mall intervened to stop the attack, throwing shoes, chairs, and other objects at the assailant before tackling and pinning him to the ground. They seized his weapon and held him until police arrived.

"An alleged unprovoked attack on anyone in our community is unacceptable, but an attack allegedly motivated because of the victim's religion is alarming."

— Sim Gill, Salt Lake County District Attorney

'A Catalyst' for Violence

Motivation Behind the Attack
›Larsen aimed to kill Muslims.
›Described as a substantial danger to the public.
›Wanted to be a catalyst for violence against Muslims.
Police Interviews

In police interviews, Larsen stated he wanted "to be a catalyst so people would rid the country of Muslims." He told investigators that if he "could go from one Muslim to another in close proximity, he would have killed as many as possible." Police described him as posing "a substantial danger to the public" based on his "violent actions, ideologies and pre-planned mass casualty events."

India's Response

The Consulate General of India in San Francisco issued a statement expressing grief over the attack. "The Consulate is in close contact with the friends and family and stands ready to provide all possible consular assistance," it said. "We remain engaged with local authorities and will continue to monitor the matter closely."

A GoFundMe fundraiser organized for Uddin's medical expenses has drawn widespread support from the community.

A Pattern of Violence

Community Response and Concerns
›GoFundMe for Uddin's medical expenses raised community support.
›Consulate General of India providing assistance.
›Incident raises safety concerns for the Indian diaspora.
Community Reactions

The attack has drawn comparisons to other recent anti-Muslim violence in the United States, including a shooting at an Islamic center in San Diego in May that left three people dead. The Council on American-Islamic Relations called the assault "yet another reminder that anti-Muslim rhetoric has real-world consequences."

For the Indian diaspora, the incident raises urgent questions about the safety of community members working in public-facing jobs across America, particularly those who may be targeted for their religious identity.
